identification.summary: Trend Micro named the actor behind this activity "DRBControl" after Talent-Jump Technologies contacted it in 2019 about a backdoor found during an incident response engagement [S1]. Trend Micro describes an APT campaign aimed at gambling and betting companies in Southeast Asia [S1]. Security Affairs reports the incident response was for a company based in the Philippines [S3].
identification.firstObserved: 2019 (Trend Micro was alerted in 2019; Dropbox expired the C2 tokens in August 2019) [S1]. Trend Micro's report was published around February 2020 per press coverage [S3].
identification.notes: This is a Trend Micro-named cluster/campaign. Trend Micro reports links to Winnti (shared mutexes, domain names, issued commands) and to Emissary Panda/APT27 (use of HyperBro, which it says appears exclusive to that group), but says the evidence is insufficient for a definitive link [S1][S4]. Do not merge facts from the Winnti, APT27 or Microsoft-named clusters into this record without vendor mapping.

attribution.confidence: Trend Micro reported overlaps with Winnti and Emissary Panda but stated there was not enough evidence to establish a definitive link [S4]. No government attribution found in sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Trend Micro cites shared mutexes, domain names and commands with Winnti, and use of the HyperBro backdoor, which it says appears exclusive to Emissary Panda [S1][S4].

objectives: Trend Micro judged the main goal to be cyberespionage, because exfiltrated data was mostly databases and source code [S1][S3].

regions: Philippines (company in the originating incident response) [S3]
Europe and Middle East reported to Trend Micro but unconfirmed [S1]
targeting.notes: Trend Micro could not confirm Europe/Middle East targeting at time of writing [S1].

capabilities.summary: Initial access via spear-phishing Word (.DOCX) documents [S1]. Two previously unidentified backdoors, one using Dropbox as its command-and-control channel [S1]. Known families including PlugX and HyperBro, plus custom post-exploitation tools [S1][S3]. Trend Micro disclosed the Dropbox C2 to Dropbox, which expired the tokens in August 2019 [S1]. CyberScoop-reported coverage also lists Trochilus RAT and Cobalt Strike per a search summary; verify against the whitepaper [S4].

diamond.adversary: Unnamed cluster tracked by Trend Micro as DRBControl, with unconfirmed overlaps to Winnti and Emissary Panda [S1][S4].

diamond.technology: Abuse of a legitimate cloud file-hosting service for C2 [S1]; Windows endpoints reached through Office document lures [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: Operation DRBControl is a cyberespionage campaign targeting gambling companies in Southeast Asia, first identified in 2019. The operation involves the use of HyperBro malware and SysUpdate variants, with evidence of customer database and source code exfiltration. The threat actor has employed domain spoofing for command and control and has shown a consistent interest in the gambling industry. Trend Micro's analysis linked multiple tools and malware families to this campaign, indicating a sophisticated and evolving threat landscape.
